restrictions: Two distinct 64-byte messages with equal digests for the Orchard hash with 25 partial rounds (poseidon-orchard-r25-prefix-v1), found as a collision F(x) = F(y), x != y, of the walk F(x) = digest(message(kappa x - E0_0)) / OUTSCALE_kappa: message() is the injective parametrisation of the input line on which rounds 0 and 1 are affine, kappa one of 4 fixed nonzero field elements drawn uniformly (the coins at which one step constant is 1), start x_0 a random 254-bit coin. Plain birthday search, one trail with distinguished points x < DELTA, one table; the success probability uses no property of the rounds.

Cost model orchard-field-ram-v2, C = 741. Prices used: canonical field ADD and MUL 1/C each; every other primitive 256-bit word operation (AND, OR, shift, compare, branch, register move, aligned load or store, random word) 1/C. No permutation call is charged as a unit: every evaluation executes the 434-operation step program (174 ADD, 260 MUL; proof.md Section 2, listing in Appendix C), an equivalent form of rounds 2-63. The per-attempt constants are computed into a declared file of 231 256-bit registers (SETUP_D = 776 operations, charged), counted in memory; arithmetic takes register operands; instructions are 4 bytes.

Ledger (proof.md Section 6, instruction listings): a trail step is 434 + 2 operations, plus 2 per block of 32 unrolled steps; a recovery evaluation at most 434 + 6, at most 3 G + d - 1 of them; table scan, insertion, bisection, constant writes, the setup, the message roots are at most 15,515,323,199 operations. The offline derivation of the constants and parameters is bounded in proof.md Section 6a by 2^48 word operations (literal PREP_OPS), inside time_log2 and also declared as preprocessing_log2 = 39 (one quantity, not added twice). time_log2 is the full budget with every halt charged at its limit: S = n + d trail steps, log2 T = 126.230449, claimed 126.23045 (rounded up). One attempt; no restart, amplification or advice.

Memory: 28,576 table entries of one 32-byte word (low 128 bits of the value in the high half, index in the low half), a side array of 16-bit high parts (1,786 words), the start word, code at most 15,179 instructions at 4 bytes, constants, the 231-register file and the per-attempt setup memory: 1,048,556 bytes, below 2^20 (proof.md Section 7; the code term and the word layout are derived there).

Success probability at least 0.39: Lemma 2 (proof.md Section 5) proves 0.39000000332006783841 (at least 0.39) for a uniformly random function at the filed budget, with explicit terms for the trail, detection, table, lockstep and positioning. H1 (the only premise, score-critical, the fixed-map premise of the published r = 23 .. 56 entries of this lineage) states that each fixed map F_kappa behaves like a uniformly random function for this search, so that the search reaches 0.39 at the filed budget; measurements at reduced width are in proof.md Section 8.

The program is printed in full in proof.md Appendix B (standard library only); the step program in Appendix C. One organizer-run experiment is declared (r25-search-w14, python-message-pairs-v1, event digest-xor-mask; source experiments/exp_search.py): the search of Section 3 on the real step program at 14 digest bits (proof.md Section 9). No full collision is produced or claimed; the claim is the cost of the search.

heuristics.statement: The filed trail has n = 133555091 * 2^100 steps, at which Lemma 2 gives 0.390000003 for a uniformly random function (the least multiple of 2^100 that reaches 0.39). Premise (H1, the fixed-map premise): each of the 4 fixed maps F_kappa(x) = digest(message(kappa x - E0_0)) / OUTSCALE_kappa behaves like a uniformly random function for the search of proof.md Section 3, so that the search with kappa drawn uniformly from the set and a uniform start succeeds with probability at least 0.39 at the budget n.
heuristics.scope: Target poseidon-orchard-r25-prefix-v1, inputs on the line of proof.md Section 1, one trail with the parameters of proof.md Section 3 (S = n + d). Applies to this round count and budget. Only the success probability rests on it; the step program, the recovery, the ledger and the memory are proved or checked exactly (proof.md Sections 2, 4, 6, 7).
heuristics.extrapolation: Support: reproducible observations consistent with the premise, not a population bound. Organizer-run experiment r25-search-w14 (python-message-pairs-v1, digest-xor-mask on the low 14 digest bits; proof.md Sections 8 and 9): the search of proof.md Section 3, unchanged, on the 4 real maps F_kappa (step program, line, coin set) at N = 2^14, parameters fixed in advance (DELTA 6144, n 176, d 16, G 16, MCAP 96). Our run on the organizer's 256 published seeds: 194 of 256 successes (mask events checked with the organizer's verifier) against the Lemma 2 random-function bound 0.43049 at those parameters; first repeat within n in 184 of 256 against the exact random-function probability 0.61485. H1 applies the random-function law to the same 4 maps at 254 bits over 2^127 steps. Sensitivity: with collision rate c times that of a random function, success is about 1 - exp(-c x) - n/N - eps with x = 0.49508; the budget reaches 0.39 only at c >= 1.000.
heuristics.limitations: H1 is a premise on 4 fixed maps, with no proof. The budget has no margin against a collision-rate deficit: it needs c >= 1.000 at full width. The organizer experiment observes the success event on the same 4 maps at 14 bits only; its trials are walks on 4 fixed maps, not independent functions, so it shows only a gross deficit at 14 bits and cannot resolve a deficit at the filed tolerance. The success bound assumes nothing about the organizer-seeded trials.
